messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Use and access.** “The Testing House may use the drawings, CAD geometry and extracts solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Only test personnel named in writing and approved by the Design Owner may access these materials. Before access, each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The same requirements apply to advisers, subcontractors and replacement personnel. The Testing House remains responsible for their compliance. Neither the Testing House nor anyone it gives access may reuse the materials or geometry derived from them to develop a competing product.”

**Copies and fixtures.** “The Testing House may make the working copies and fixture designs reasonably necessary for the agreed tests and may fabricate fixtures from those designs. It must encrypt the files in storage and in transit, restrict physical access to the fixtures to approved personnel, and keep a record of copies and fixtures. The final report may retain test results and measurements but must exclude CAD geometry and extracts from the drawings unless the Design Owner approves their inclusion in writing.”

**Destruction and verification.** “Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the test work, the Testing House must securely erase all drawings, working copies and geometry-bearing derivative files in its control and destroy all geometry-bearing fixtures made for the tests. Within the same period, it must provide a certificate from an independent verifier who has checked the copy and fixture record and the evidence of destruction. The certificate must identify the materials covered, the destruction methods and dates, and any exceptions. The Design Owner has no routine right of site entry.”

Can your quality system retain the report and test measurements while deleting the geometry-bearing files within 30 days? If a specific accreditation or backup requirement prevents that, please identify the affected records and the shortest required retention period so we can agree a narrow exception.

Yes, we can retain the final report and test measurements while deleting geometry-bearing files within 30 days. Our quality system stores measurement data, results, and fixture/test-setup logs separately from CAD geometry and drawing extracts. On the 30-day schedule we will securely erase all geometry-bearing files, derivatives, and geometry-bearing fixtures, and we will keep the report and measurements intact.

There is one narrow retention point tied to our accreditation. The accredited lab and the specialist machining shop must keep calibration and setup records for two years to maintain accreditation and measurement traceability. Those records reference fixture IDs, sensor mounts, load frames, and test parameters, but they do not contain CAD geometry or drawing extracts. We can accept the 30-day deletion for geometry-bearing materials and carve out a time-limited retention of non-geometry calibration/setup records for two years. If any accreditation requirement forces us to keep a geometry-linked fixture configuration file for traceability, we will retain only a redacted metadata record (IDs, dates, tolerances, revision identifiers) and destroy the geometry. We will document that scope in the certificate so the exception is visible and narrow.

The draft covers replacement personnel but does not give us a workable substitution path mid-job. We need an explicit mechanism so we can swap a vibration specialist or a machining technician during the test campaign without breaking access rules. We propose adding a substitution clause that requires written notice to the Design Owner, confirmation that the replacement is bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement before any access, and that the replacement steps into the same named-personnel slot for the remaining work. The Testing House remains responsible for the replacement’s compliance. No new access categories or broader rights are created by the swap.

On verification, an independent verifier certificate for all copies and fixtures is acceptable for geometry-bearing items. For the non-geometry records we retain (report, measurements, two-year calibration logs), our accredited QA system can provide a destruction/retention attestation with chain-of-custody and audit logs, which meets the verification intent without requiring an external verifier for every document. Tradeoff: if you require an independent verifier for the full scope, we will limit the certificate to geometry-bearing files and geometry-bearing fixtures and supply our QA attestation for the retained calibration logs. That keeps geometry protection intact while avoiding disproportionate cost and delay on records that never contain geometry.

We also agree that the Design Owner has no routine right of site entry, and we will not permit unannounced inspections at any shared or customer site. If you need physical confirmation that geometry-bearing fixtures were destroyed, we can arrange a single scheduled joint confirmation or accept documented evidence from the machining shop and lab. Routine or unannounced entry is not workable for us.

**Proposed replacement wording**

1. **Specialist substitution.** “If the Testing House needs to substitute a named test specialist or machining technician during the agreed work, it will give the Design Owner written notice identifying the replacement and the effective date. The replacement will not access the drawings, CAD geometry, or extracts until bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House remains fully responsible for the replacement’s compliance. The substitution does not create new access rights or change the scope of permitted use.”

2. **Narrow retention exception.** “Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the test work, the Testing House will securely erase all drawings, working copies, and geometry-bearing derivative files in its control and destroy all geometry-bearing fixtures made for the tests. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Testing House may retain calibration and test-setup records required by its accredited lab and machining shop for two years. Those retained records will not contain CAD geometry or drawing extracts; where a fixture configuration file is required for traceability, only a redacted metadata record will be kept. The certificate of destruction will identify any such non-geometry records retained, their retention period, and the reason for retention.”

3. **Verification scope.** “Within the same 30-day period, the Testing House will provide a certificate from an independent verifier who has checked the copy and fixture record and the evidence of destruction for the drawings, working copies, geometry-bearing derivative files, and geometry-bearing fixtures. For test reports, measurements, and any retained two-year calibration logs that do not contain geometry, the Testing House will provide a quality-system attestation with chain-of-custody and audit evidence of deletion or retention. The certificate will identify the materials covered, the destruction methods and dates, and any exceptions. The Design Owner has no routine right of site entry; physical confirmation of fixture destruction, if requested, will be scheduled in advance or accepted via documented evidence from the machining shop and lab.”

**Tradeoffs we are testing**
- 30-day geometry deletion plus two-year non-geometry calibration retention: yes, workable; we only need the exception documented and narrow.
- Independent verifier for geometry-bearing items only, with QA attestation for retained non-geometry records: yes, this protects geometry without slowing or over-costing the retention of accreditation logs. If you require full independent verification, we will accept it but it will extend cost and timeline for records that already exclude geometry.
- Substitution notice + pre-access confidentiality bind: required for us to run the job without risking access breaches or schedule loss.

Please confirm whether the two-year non-geometry retention exception and the scoped verification approach are acceptable, and whether the substitution wording closes the gap for your side. If you need the independent verifier to cover all materials, tell us which records you want included so we can price the timeline impact and adjust the certificate scope accordingly.

We accept the two-year retention exception and the proposed verification scope. The substitution clause works with one change: each person who can access the geometry needs our written approval. We can approve named alternates before testing begins so a mid-job substitution can take effect on notice.

**Specialist substitution.** “The Design Owner may approve named alternates in writing for specified roles. To activate an approved alternate, the Testing House will give written notice identifying the outgoing person, the alternate, the role and the effective time. For anyone outside the approved list, the Testing House must obtain the Design Owner’s written approval before granting access. The Design Owner will respond promptly to substitution requests. Before the replacement receives access, the Testing House will confirm that the replacement is bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement and will revoke the outgoing person’s access. The replacement may use the materials only for the approved role and the remaining agreed work. The Testing House remains responsible for compliance.”

**Retention.** The lab and machining shop may retain required calibration and setup records for two years from the relevant test date, then delete them. A redacted record may retain identifiers, dates, tolerances and revision references only to the extent that they do not reveal or allow reconstruction of the geometry. The 30-day destruction obligation includes geometry held by the lab and shop. The final report and measurements may be kept as agreed.

**Verification.** We accept independent certification for geometry-bearing materials and fixtures only. Documented destruction evidence from the shop and lab is sufficient for the verifier’s review. The day-30 QA attestation may cover the retained non-geometry records and identify the basis and deletion date for each category of two-year records. A QA attestation after deletion will close out those records. Any physical confirmation would require separate mutual agreement and advance scheduling.

The agreed test-only use, encrypted working copies, fixture limits and prohibition on reuse to develop competing products continue to apply to every substitute. Can you confirm the approved-alternate mechanism and the retention closeout on that basis?

We accept the two-business-day response target and the proposed lab and shop scope. We agree to finalization with the following wording added to the substitution clause.

“The Design Owner will aim to respond in writing within two business days of receiving a request identifying the proposed replacement and role. If the person already has written approval as an alternate for that role, the Testing House may activate the alternate on written notice once it has met the agreed confidentiality and access-transfer requirements. For any other replacement, access requires the Design Owner’s express written approval. Expiry of the response window does not constitute approval.

“The same substitution, written approval, pre-access confidentiality and use restrictions apply to all accredited lab and machining shop personnel who access geometry-bearing materials or fixtures.”

We agree to the retention and verification terms as drafted. The independent certificate and QA attestations satisfy our verification requirements. Any physical confirmation requires separate mutual agreement and advance scheduling.

We can run the stock, coupon measurement, tolerance table, and fixture build inside the agreed access and deletion terms, with a bounded two-day handoff and a clear signoff sequence. Here is what we need from your side to lock it.

**Custody of stock and geometry-linked parts.**  
The machining shop already has stock cut to the original fixture design. We treat that stock and any interim fixture parts as geometry-bearing material for custody purposes while they are in transit or on the test floor. We propose:
- A short custody log for any movement of geometry-linked stock or fixture components between the shop and the testing house, with file/part identifiers, dates, and responsible personnel.
- Encryption and access controls matching the agreement while files or geometry-linked parts are in our control.
- No geometry-bearing stock or fixture leaves our control except for the agreed fabrication/assembly step, and any temporary transfer is logged and time-bound.

**Tolerances and repeatability check.**  
We will measure a reference coupon at the testing house and send the shop a tolerance table. To do that without delay or rework, we need:
- The designer to specify the tolerance table in writing (dimensions, acceptable variation, datum scheme, and any surface or assembly constraints tied to the fixture).
- Acceptance of a repeatability check on the coupon before the shop releases final fixture build. Our proposed check: a small set of repeated measurements on the same coupon under the same setup, with the spread compared to the specified tolerance. If the spread sits inside the tolerance band, the table is issued and the shop proceeds. If it falls outside, we flag it for revision and pause the build until the tolerance spec or method is adjusted.

**Two-day delay.**  
The two days cover coupon measurement, tolerance table generation, and shop review of that table before fixture build. We propose:
- The delay starts on the day the designer issues the written tolerance spec and the coupon is available at the testing house.
- Within two business days we deliver the tolerance table to the shop and confirm repeatability acceptance or flag an exception.
- This two-day window does not reset the 30-day geometry deletion clock. That clock still runs from written acceptance of the final test report, or from earlier termination of the test work, as already agreed.
- If the tolerance spec is late or the repeatability check fails, the clock for the two-day handoff pauses until the spec is fixed and the check is repeated. We will document the pause and resumption in the custody log.

**Test signoff.**  
We propose a staged signoff that keeps the geometry controls and verification terms intact:
1. Designer issues written tolerance spec.
2. Testing house measures the reference coupon and issues the tolerance table to the shop, with repeatability acceptance noted.
3. Shop fabricates/verifies the fixture against the table; geometry-linked parts remain under logged custody until assembled for the vibration tests.
4. Vibration tests run with named or approved-alternate personnel only.
5. Final test report and measurements issued; geometry-bearing files, derivatives, and geometry-bearing fixtures fall under the 30-day deletion obligation; retained non-geometry calibration/setup records follow the two-year retention with redacted metadata only.

**Tradeoffs we are testing**
- If you want the shop to submit fixture metrology before build, we can add that step. It reduces rework risk but extends the schedule beyond the two-day handoff.
- If you accept our repeatability check plus the tolerance table, we keep the two-day delay bounded and avoid holding the job, while still protecting geometry during custody and build.
- If you prefer a tighter custody regime, we can require that geometry-linked stock and fixture parts stay at the shop until the tolerance table is accepted, then move only what is needed for assembly. That reduces on-site geometry exposure but adds a transfer step and log.

**What we need from you to close this**
- Written tolerance spec format and the dimensions/variation/datum basis for the fixture, in time for the coupon measurement.
- Confirmation that a repeatability check on the reference coupon is acceptable before the shop releases final fixture build, and the acceptance band or method if you want it specified.
- Confirmation that the two-day handoff runs from tolerance spec issue and does not alter the 30-day deletion clock tied to final report acceptance or termination.
- Agreement on the custody log scope for geometry-linked stock and fixture parts during transit and on the test floor.

Once those points are confirmed, we can start the coupon measurement, issue the tolerance table within the two-day window, and proceed to fixture build and vibration testing under the access, substitution, retention, and verification terms already agreed.

We request a narrow addendum for this prototype batch. Only the geometry on page 4 is export-restricted. We propose using an alternative reference coupon for the fixture work. Work that uses only released material from the other pages may proceed.

**Page 4 and existing stock.** “The Design Owner will withhold page 4 and supply a drawing set with the restricted geometry removed. The Testing House and shop may use only the released set, coupon and approved tolerance table for this batch. The shop will segregate the stock already cut to the original design and any related interim parts. Pending written disposition from the Design Owner, those items must stay at the shop and must not be measured, machined or transferred. If either facility already holds page 4 or a derivative, it will isolate the material and notify the Design Owner by identifier and location without transmitting the geometry.”

**Coupon and verification.** We need two business days **from written agreement on the verification test** to prepare the coupon and its specification. We will release both after checking that neither reveals or permits reconstruction of the page 4 geometry. The specification will give one row per coupon feature, with its identifier, nominal dimension, units, upper and lower limits, datum, measurement method, maximum permitted repeatability spread, and any applicable surface or assembly constraint. The actual values will come from our project engineer.

We propose three independent measurements per feature, removing and reseating the coupon against the specified datum between readings. Each reading must fall within the feature limits, and the difference between the highest and lowest readings must meet the specified spread limit. This checks both dimensional acceptance and repeatability of the seating. Please send the completed table to us for written release **before it goes to the shop**. A failed feature holds the build pending written resolution and a passing recheck.

**Handoff and custody.** Your separate two-business-day handoff starts when the testing house has both the released coupon and the written specification. Within that window, send us the completed table or identify the exception. Record any pause and resumption. After written release, the shop may build against the table and verify the finished fixture before use. We accept a custody log covering dispatch, receipt, test-floor handoffs and final disposition, recording item identifiers, dates, locations and responsible named personnel. Only released items needed for assembly may move. Files remain encrypted and physical items remain under controlled custody.

The existing 30-day destruction deadline still runs from written acceptance of the final report or earlier termination. The independent certificate must account for the original stock and interim parts as well as the completed fixture. The two-year retention exception covers only the agreed non-geometry records.

Please confirm that the shop can hold the original stock in place, identify whether either facility already holds page 4 or a derivative, and confirm the reseating test and written table-release step. That agreement starts our two-day preparation period.

We can confirm the following on our side and propose two narrow clarifications so the two-day preparation period can start cleanly.

**Shop holding original stock in place.** Yes. Our machining shop will quarantine the already-cut stock and any related interim parts to the original design. Those items will stay at the shop, will not be measured, machined, or transferred, and will remain under controlled custody pending your written disposition. We will record identifiers, location, responsible personnel, and the quarantine date.

**Current holdings of page 4 or derivatives.** We will check our records now. If either facility already holds page 4 or a derivative, we will isolate it and notify you by identifier and location without transmitting the geometry, as proposed. If we do not hold it, we will confirm that in writing when the addendum takes effect.

**Reseating test and written table-release step.** We accept the three-measurement approach: one reading per feature per seating, with the coupon removed and reseated against the specified datum between readings. Each reading must fall within the feature limits, and the difference between the highest and lowest reading must meet the specified repeatability spread limit. We will send the completed table to you for written release before anything goes to the shop. A failed feature will hold the build pending your written resolution and a passing recheck using the same method, limits, and spread criteria.

**Trigger for your two-day preparation period.** We agree the period starts from your written agreement on the verification test. To avoid ambiguity, we propose that “written agreement on the verification test” means a written sign-off on the verification test scope and the coupon/spec requirements, not on the measured values themselves.

**Safeguard on actual values.** Because the specification will carry actual values from your project engineer, we propose that those actual values be limited to functional/seating offsets, clearances, and coupon-specific measurements, and must not reference drawing geometry, coordinates, or any feature that would allow reconstruction of the page 4 geometry. If that is acceptable, the table will remain non-geometry by construction. If you intend the actual values to capture something closer to geometry, we need to narrow or redact those fields before release.

**Custody, encryption, and item movement.** We will maintain the custody log covering dispatch, receipt, test-floor handoffs, and final disposition, recording item identifiers, dates, locations, and responsible named personnel. Files remain encrypted in storage and in transit. Only released items needed for assembly may move. After written release, the shop may build against the table and verify the finished fixture before use.

**Destruction, retention, and certificate scope.** The 30-day destruction deadline continues to run from written acceptance of the final report or earlier termination. The independent certificate must account for the original stock, interim parts, and the completed fixture, without geometry. The two-year retention exception covers only the agreed non-geometry records, and those will be deleted at the end of the period. We will ensure the custody log feeds the certificate so the stock, interim parts, and fixture are traceable without revealing geometry.

**Tradeoffs we are testing**
- Your two-day prep window tied to written agreement on the verification test is workable if the trigger is scope/requirements sign-off rather than acceptance of measured values.
- Limiting actual values to functional/seating offsets and clearances keeps the table non-geometry and avoids a reconstruction risk. If you need broader values, we will require written redaction or a non-geometry-only release before the shop sees it.
- Build hold on a failed feature plus a passing recheck is acceptable and aligns with our fixture verification practice.

**What we need from you to start**
1. Confirm the trigger definition for “written agreement on the verification test” as scope/requirements sign-off.
2. Confirm the actual-values safeguard (functional/seating offsets and clearances only, no geometry references) or specify any fields that must be excluded/redacted before release.
3. Tell us whether you will provide the written release of the completed table before it goes to the shop, and whether any interim shop access must be blocked until that release is in hand.

Once those are aligned, we will confirm our internal page 4/derivative check and quarantine status, and your two-day preparation period can begin.

We accept both clarifications. **This message is our written sign-off on the verification test scope and the coupon and specification requirements. Our two-business-day preparation period starts now.** Your separate two-business-day measurement window begins when the testing house has received both the released coupon and its written specification.

The specification and table may contain functional seating offsets, clearances and coupon-specific measurements, with the coupon datums and limits needed for the agreed three-seating test. Both documents must exclude page 4 geometry, drawing coordinates and any combination of values that would permit reconstruction of the restricted geometry.

**We will review the completed table and issue its release in writing.** Until that release, the shop must have no access to the coupon, specification, draft table or measurement results for this fixture. A failed feature holds the build pending written resolution and a passing recheck. Release of the table authorizes fabrication against that version only. The original stock and interim parts remain quarantined pending separate written disposition.

Please send the written holdings check for both facilities and the shop’s quarantine confirmation when available, using identifiers and locations only. Coupon preparation can proceed while you complete that check.

We accept your written sign-off on the verification test scope and the coupon and specification requirements. We will proceed on the timeline you set: our two-business-day preparation period starts now, and our separate two-business-day measurement window begins when we have received both the released coupon and its written specification.

We will prepare the specification and table to contain functional seating offsets, clearances, and coupon-specific measurements, together with the coupon datums and limits needed for the agreed three-seating test. Both documents will exclude page 4 geometry, drawing coordinates, and any combination of values that would permit reconstruction of the restricted geometry. We will not release the table or specification until your written review and release.

Access controls: Until your written release of the table, the shop will have no access to the coupon, specification, draft table, or measurement results for this fixture. A failed feature will hold the build pending written resolution and a passing recheck. Release of the table authorizes fabrication against that version only. Original stock and interim parts will remain quarantined pending separate written disposition.

We will send, when available, the written holdings check for both facilities and the shop’s quarantine confirmation, using identifiers and locations only. Coupon preparation can proceed in parallel while we complete that check.

If you need the holdings check to cover any specific record categories beyond identifiers and locations, tell us now so we can include them before we send.

One correction for the addendum: **the Design Owner’s project engineer prepares the coupon and writes the specification, including the actual values, during our two-business-day preparation period.** That period began with our written sign-off. We will release both items to the testing house. Receipt of both starts your two-business-day window to perform the three-seating test and return the completed table or report a failed feature. We will review the completed table and authorize the specific version in writing before the shop receives it.

For the holdings check, please cover page 4 and its derivatives at each facility, including electronic files, working copies and paper drawings or extracts. Identifiers and locations are sufficient for any holdings. If a facility finds none, please say so expressly. The separate quarantine confirmation covers the original stock and interim parts.

We accept the clarified flow. Below is our confirmation, the operational points we need to pin down, and the tradeoffs we are testing to keep the timeline and verification workable.

**Confirmed process**
- The project engineer prepares the coupon and writes the specification, including actual values, during the two-business-day preparation period that began on your written sign-off.
- You release both the coupon and the specification to us. Receipt of both starts our two-business-day window to perform the three-seating test and return either the completed table or a failed-feature report.
- We will not release anything to the shop until you have reviewed the completed table and authorized the specific version in writing.
- Holdings check covers page 4 and its derivatives at each facility, across electronic files, working copies, and paper drawings or extracts. Identifiers and locations are sufficient; any facility that finds none will state that expressly.
- The separate quarantine confirmation covers original stock and interim parts and remains distinct from the holdings check.

**Points we need to align to run this without ambiguity**
1. **Start trigger for the two-business-day window.** We propose that “receipt” means a dated delivery record we can evidence (e.g., signed handoff, secure email with read receipt, or portal upload confirmation). That removes dispute over when the clock starts. If you prefer a different trigger, tell us the exact event and we will bind to it.
2. **Output format for the completed table / failed-feature report.** We will return a table with the three-seating results and any measured values against the specification, or a failed-feature report that identifies the feature, the observed result, and the deviation. Please confirm whether you want the table to include pass/fail per seat, raw readings, and the signature/approval line that precedes your written version authorization. If the format is fixed, we will match it exactly.
3. **Risk of missing the two-business-day window.** The three-seating test itself can fit within the window, but if setup, fixture mating, or equipment availability would push us past it, we will notify you at the start of day one with the reason and a proposed path (for example, partial completion with placeholder rows, or a same-day reschedule). Expiry of the window without notice is not our intended operating mode; we will treat day-two end-of-day as the deadline for the completed table or failed-feature report unless you instruct otherwise.
4. **Holdings check reporting.** We will provide a per-facility list showing page 4 and each derivative, the media type, and the location or storage path. If a facility holds none, we will state “No holdings of page 4 or its derivatives found” for that facility. We can deliver this on a fixed cadence (for example, within one business day of request) or tied to a defined checkpoint. Please confirm the timing you want.
5. **Quarantine confirmation scope.** We will keep it separate and cover original stock and interim parts only, with identifiers, quantities, locations, and the quarantine status. It will not merge into the page-4 holdings check.

**Tradeoffs we are testing**
- Fixed two-business-day window starting on a provable receipt event: workable if the spec and coupon are complete and the test setup is ready. If setup can be blocked by fixture readiness or equipment booking, a same-day notice clause protects both sides without diluting the deadline.
- Table format aligned to your review step: we prefer a defined template so the completed table maps directly to your written version authorization and avoids rework before shop release.
- Holdings check as a one-day turnaround per request with explicit “none found” statements: keeps verification lightweight and auditable without requiring full content review.

If the above reflects your side, we will bind to receipt-triggered timing, the agreed table/failed-feature output, pre-shop written authorization, the page-4 holdings check with explicit “none found” statements, and the separate quarantine confirmation. Tell us which receipt trigger and table format you want, and whether you prefer a one-day turnaround for the holdings check or a checkpoint-based cadence. Once those are set, we can treat the addendum as finalized on this basis.

We agree to finalize the addendum on the following terms.

1. **Receipt and deadline.** The measurement window starts at the later of two recorded events: signed delivery of the released coupon to named testing-house personnel and confirmed delivery of the released specification through the agreed secure channel. The specification delivery record must identify the version and show that the file is accessible to the named recipient. The completed table or failed-feature report is due by close of business at the testing house on the second business day following that trigger.

2. **Results format.** Identify the coupon, specification version and table version. Use one row per coupon feature with its identifier, unit, limits, three raw readings in seating order, pass/fail for each reading, observed spread, permitted spread and overall feature result. For a failed feature, identify the criterion missed and the amount of deviation. Include the named tester’s dated sign-off. Our separate written authorization will identify the exact table version the shop may use. The agreed exclusions for page 4 apply to every field and attachment.

3. **Delay or incomplete testing.** Flag a known scheduling risk at the start of day one and any later issue as soon as it becomes known. Identify the affected measurements, reason and proposed completion time. We can agree a revised deadline in writing. Pending that agreement, the original deadline applies. Mark unmeasured features “untested.” A partial table is a progress record only. Fabrication remains on hold until all features pass and we release the completed version in writing.

4. **Holdings and quarantine.** Send the holdings check and separate quarantine confirmation within one business day of this message. For each facility, list the identifier, media type and location of each page 4 holding or derivative, or expressly state that none were found. Isolate any holding immediately and report it without transmitting its contents. The quarantine confirmation should give the identifiers, quantities, locations and status of the original stock and interim parts. They remain at the shop pending our separate written disposition.

The Design Owner’s two-business-day coupon preparation period continues from the original sign-off.

We accept the finalization terms and can execute on them on our side. Our confirmation and the precise points we will lock in before sign-off:

**1. Measurement window and deadline.**  
We accept the trigger as the later of: signed delivery of the released coupon to our named testing-house personnel; and confirmed delivery of the released specification through the agreed secure channel, with a delivery record identifying the version and showing accessibility to the named recipient. The completed table or failed-feature report is due by close of business at the testing house on the second business day following that trigger. We will record both trigger events with date-time evidence and use the later event to start the clock.

**2. Results format.**  
We will produce the table with one row per coupon feature: identifier, unit, limits, three raw readings in seating order, pass/fail per reading, observed spread, permitted spread, and overall feature result. For a failed feature we will identify the criterion missed and the amount of deviation. The table will carry the coupon, specification version, and table version, plus the named tester’s dated sign-off. The shop will use only the table version you separately authorize in writing. The agreed page 4 exclusions apply to every field and attachment. We will keep the table version consistent with your written authorization and will not advance a new table version without that authorization.

**3. Delay or incomplete testing.**  
We accept the delay discipline: flag any known scheduling risk at the start of day one, and any later issue as soon as it becomes known; identify the affected measurements, the reason, and the proposed completion time; and leave the original deadline in place until you agree a revised deadline in writing. Unmeasured features will be marked “untested,” and a partial table will be treated as a progress record only. Fabrication stays on hold until all features pass and you release the completed version in writing.

**4. Holdings and quarantine.**  
We will send the holdings check and the separate quarantine confirmation within one business day of this message. For each facility, the holdings check will list the identifier, media type, and location of each page 4 holding or derivative, or expressly state that none were found. Any holding found will be isolated immediately and reported without transmitting its contents. The quarantine confirmation will give the identifiers, quantities, locations, and status of the original stock and interim parts. Those items remain at the shop pending your separate written disposition.

**Clarifications we need to close cleanly**

On “page 4,” we need a fixed document and version reference so the shop and our testers apply the same exclusions. We propose a short cross-reference sentence:

“References to ‘page 4’ mean page 4 of the [named document] at version [X], as in effect for the relevant coupon and specification version, together with any exclusions attached to that page in writing by the Design Owner. No field or attachment on that page may be used to reproduce or infer geometry or design intent, and any excluded content is omitted from the table, attachments, and distributed records.”

If you already have a preferred document and version label, give us the exact reference and we will use it. If you prefer the exclusion list attached rather than page-referenced, we can switch the wording to an attached exclusions schedule.

On the secure-channel delivery record, we will capture: recipient name, version identifier, a delivery timestamp from the channel, and a confirmation that the recipient can open the file. If you want a specific field set for the record, we can align to it; otherwise we will use that minimal evidence set.

On the tester sign-off, we will use the named tester assigned for the measurement role, and we will not substitute a signer without following the substitution clause we already agreed. That keeps the sign-off tied to the approved personnel scope.

**Tradeoffs we are testing here**
- Trigger method: later of receipt events, with documented evidence on both sides, is workable.
